data_objects.name: France genotype bundle
data_objects.meaning: A PLINK-style genotype dataset whose BED binary call matrix is indexed by the ordered variant records in the BIM file and the ordered sample records in either byte-identical FAM file.

data_objects.name: Naples genotype bundle
data_objects.meaning: A PLINK-style genotype dataset with a BED binary call matrix, an ordered BIM variant table, two FAM sample-table versions, and a headered backup representation of the BIM variant table.

data_objects.name: France group summary
data_objects.meaning: Seven group-level records containing a group code, average latitude and longitude, a sample count, and a filtered variant count.

structure.description: France_Group.bed begins with PLINK BED magic bytes 6c 1b and orientation byte 01. Excluding the header-like first FAM row leaves 256 ordered sample records, and France_Group.bim has 520,564 ordered variant rows. The 33,316,099-byte BED size equals 3 + 520,564 × ceil(256/4), consistent with variant-major packing aligned to those two axes.

France_Group.fam and France_Group_updated.fam are byte-identical 257-line files: one header-like row followed by 256 sample records. The first header cell is French rather than a field label, while the remaining five cells name the other columns.

Naples_Group.bed has the same PLINK magic bytes and orientation byte 01. Excluding the FAM header-like row leaves eight ordered sample records, and Naples_Group.bim has 564,353 ordered variant rows. The 1,128,709-byte BED size equals 3 + 564,353 × ceil(8/4), consistent with variant-major packing aligned to those axes.

Naples_Group.bim.orig contains a six-field header followed by content byte-identical to the headerless Naples_Group.bim. Naples_Group.fam and Naples_Group_updated.fam contain the same eight sample records and differ only in the first header cell: family_id in the former and Naples in the latter.

Within each PLINK bundle, BIM row order defines the BED variant axis and FAM data-record order defines the BED sample axis. The France and Naples bundles have separate sample and variant dimensions; the public artifacts do not assert row-wise alignment between the two bundles.

The seven France group-summary rows have num_samples values summing to 256, matching the France FAM sample count, and every filtered_SNP_count value is 520,564, matching the France BIM variant count. No public field directly maps an individual_id to a Group code.

uncertainties: No genome build, chromosome-code convention, coordinate reference metadata, or strand convention is supplied for either variant table.
The unit of genetic_position is not stated in the public artifacts.

The two BIM allele columns are not identified as reference/alternate, effect/non-effect, ancestral/derived, or otherwise biologically oriented; the meaning of the observed zero allele code is also unspecified.
The meanings of FAM sex and phenotype codes and of zero-valued parental identifiers are not documented, so conventional PLINK interpretations were not assigned.
BED genotype payloads were not decoded; genotype-call distributions, missing-call occurrence, and dataset-specific semantic treatment of missing calls remain unknown.

The filenames indicate original or updated sidecars, but the public artifacts do not explicitly declare which version is canonical. The observable equivalences and header differences are recorded without selecting one.

The France summary counts align in aggregate with the France genotype dimensions, but no sample-to-Group membership key is present, so the seven group codes cannot be joined to individual records from the public files alone.
annotation_notes: Evidence was limited to the permitted public descendants and the routed population-genetics reference.

Inspection covered the file inventory, line and field counts, bounded representative BIM/FAM/CSV rows, sidecar comparisons, and the first three BED bytes plus size/dimension consistency; no genotype payload was decoded or analyzed.
Names assigned to headerless BIM columns follow the observed six-column PLINK structure and the routed format reference.
